title: Code Buddy
tagline: Autonomous AI coding agent using TypeSafe JEV and LiteLLM for GitHub issue resolution
overview: Code Buddy is a Python service that polls a GitHub repository for open issues, classifies each eligible issue, and routes it to a focused AI specialist. The specialists investigate the repository and open pull requests autonomously.
problem: General-purpose local coding assistants lack bounded context and safety rails when operating on repositories, leading to unpredictable changes.
solution: Built around bounded, purpose-specific agents (repo-explorer, coder, pr-agent) using GitHub API operations guarded by strict middleware and human approval flows.

architecture.diagram: GitHub -> Orchestrator -> TypeSafe JEV -> LiteLLM -> Specialist (Coder/Repo-Explorer/PR-Agent) -> Guardrails -> GitHub
architecture.notes: Uses TypeSafe JEV for structured classification without invoking the coding LLM. Models are routed via LiteLLM based on agent role to optimize costs.

challenges.challenge: Agents performing unsafe operations or running destructive commands
challenges.resolution: Implemented guardrails with deterministic checks (sensitive paths, dangerous commands) and TypeSafe JEV semantic checks.

title: Autonomous AI Researcher
tagline: Multi-agent system for comprehensive academic research generation
overview: An AI agent system that accepts a research topic, autonomously browses academic databases, synthesizes findings, and produces a cited literature review.
problem: Literature reviews are time-consuming and often miss emerging research papers due to human oversight.
solution: A pipeline of specialized agents (Searcher, Reader, Synthesizer, Reviewer) working in tandem to produce high-quality reviews.

architecture.diagram: User Input -> Planner Agent -> Worker Agents -> Synthesis -> Output
architecture.notes: Orchestrated using LangGraph for cyclic agent workflows and state management.

challenges.resolution: Added a strict verification step requiring every claim to map back to a retrieved context window chunk.

title: E-Commerce Microservices
tagline: Event-driven backend architecture for a high-traffic retail platform
overview: A scalable backend system replacing a monolithic e-commerce application, built to handle flash sales and high throughput.
problem: The old monolith crashed during Black Friday sales due to database locking and tight coupling.
solution: Decomposed into Orders, Inventory, Users, and Payment services communicating asynchronously via Apache Kafka.

architecture.diagram: API Gateway -> Services -> Kafka -> Event Handlers
architecture.notes: Leveraged Kafka for event sourcing to ensure no data loss during service outages.

challenges.resolution: Implemented the Saga pattern using choreography to handle rollbacks gracefully if payment failed.

title: MediBot Assistant RAG Pipeline
tagline: Secure retrieval-augmented generation for internal company documents
overview: MediAssist is a role-aware hospital knowledge assistant. It combines a polished Next.js chat interface with a FastAPI retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) service, local Qdrant vector storage, SQL-backed operational data, and a Groq-powered language model.
problem: Employees spent hours searching through Confluence and internal wikis to find standard operating procedures or medical bills patient records.
solution: Ingested 10,000+ internal documents into a Hybrid dense and sparse vector retrieval through Qdrant, wrapped in a conversational UI/ChatBot with strict role-based access control.

architecture.diagram: Documents -> Text Splitter -> Embedding Model -> Pinecone <- FastAPI <- UI
architecture.notes: Uses metadata filtering in Pinecone to enforce access controls before passing context to the LLM.

challenges.challenge: Poor retrieval quality on domain-specific acronyms
challenges.resolution: Implemented hybrid search combining sparse (BM25) and dense embeddings, significantly improving recall.
